evals.prompt: In Python, drive articulation DOF velocity targets, step, then read the joint velocities back.
evals.expected_output: Warms up or steps first, opens a PhysX.write session on jointVelocityTarget, fills every tensor of every group and commits, steps, then reads jointVelocity (a state attribute) back; does not use tensor bindings.
expectations: Warms up or steps before opening the write session
Fills every tensor of every group before commit, and asserts at least one group committed
Reads the outcome from a state attribute (jointVelocity), not the target it wrote

evals.prompt: My PhysX.write() call right after loading the stage commits but nothing moves. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains the session write is refused before the first step and does not auto-warm; call warmup() or step_sync() before the write.
expectations: Explains a pre-step write is refused / not applied, and the write never auto-warms
Tells the caller to warmup() or step first, then write

evals.prompt: I want to apply a force at a specific world point on a rigid body with the write API, not at its center of mass.
evals.expected_output: Uses the wrench attribute (force, torque, world application point), not force (which is COM-only); notes it is write-only so the effect is observed as motion, not read back.
expectations: Uses wrench with the [fx,fy,fz, tx,ty,tz, px,py,pz] layout, not force
Explains force is applied at the center of mass while wrench carries the application point
Notes force/wrench are write-only: assert the consequence, do not read the load back

evals.prompt: Read rigid-body poses back while keeping ovstage prim identity and attribute tokens for a closed-loop write-back.
evals.expected_output: Routes to ovphysx-output-read for the read side rather than the write skill.
expectations: Does not select ovphysx-session-write for reading output back

evals.prompt: I have legacy code that reads and writes simulation state as caller-owned NumPy arrays through create_tensor_binding. What is the non-deprecated replacement for the write side?
evals.expected_output: Points at the session write API (PhysX.write / ovphysx_write) covered by ovphysx-session-write as the successor to the deprecated tensor-binding write.
expectations: Identifies the tensor-binding API as deprecated
Selects ovphysx-session-write as the successor for the write side
